name: Jaimie Branch
label: International Anthem
lede: A trumpeter who played Chicago's Velvet Lounge as a teenager, rebuilt her life in Brooklyn, and made the loudest, most danceable free-jazz records of the 2010s. Her last one came out a year after she died.

eras.title: A trumpet at nine, a suburb at fourteen
eras.text: Born on Long Island, raised on the trumpet, and dropped into the Chicago suburbs just in time to sneak into the city's improvised-music rooms. Everything later, the punk volume and the jazz chops, comes from these two places.

years.src: NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary · Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch
years.h: Jaimie Branch is born in Huntington, New York
years.p: She starts on piano at three and trumpet at nine, according to NPR's obituary.
years.xp: NPR reports she later studied at the New England Conservatory in Boston with trumpet teacher Charles Schlueter and improvisers [[Joe Morris|a9527992-99db-46c3-a2aa-abab9c36e90e]] and John McNeil. She worked on circular breathing and multiphonics, the extended techniques that later let one trumpet sound like a small brass section.

years.src: NPR: Chicago trumpeter jaimie branch delivers · The Quietus
years.h: A teenager in the front row at Velvet Lounge and Lounge Ax
years.p: Her family moves to Wilmette, Illinois, and she starts going into Chicago to hear improvised music and rock, NPR's local station reports.
years.xp: At fourteen Branch moved to the Chicago suburbs. Per NPR's Chicago coverage of her second album, she was hanging around rooms like Velvet Lounge and Lounge Ax as a teen, a free-jazz club and a rock club a few miles apart. The Quietus later quoted her describing Chicago as a melting pot of free jazz, punk, blues, hip hop, house and West African traditions, which is a fair description of her records.

eras.title: Chicago takes her in
eras.text: After Boston she came back to a city where a young trumpeter could play with Ken Vandermark and Nicole Mitchell. A detour to Baltimore and a hard stretch ended with a one-way move to Brooklyn.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch
years.h: First record credit: The Art of Dying with Jason Ajemian
years.p: Wikipedia lists her on bassist [[Jason Ajemian|c9fd3164-ef5e-4a91-b1da-ef7ee96ddba2]]'s 2006 record, the start of a partnership that ran to her last album.
years.xp: Ajemian and Branch both ended up in Chicago's improvised-music scene. He would be the bassist in every lineup of Fly or Die, and in the 2023 bandmates' statement he is one of the voices remembering her.

years.src: NPR: Chicago trumpeter jaimie branch delivers · NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary
years.h: Back from Boston, into Keefe Jackson's Project Project
years.p: Branch returns to Chicago for good, and plays on Keefe Jackson's Just Like This the same year.
years.xp: NPR says she moved back permanently in 2007 after studying in Boston. She also appeared at the Festival of New Trumpet Music that year, per NPR's obituary.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch
years.h: Tim Daisy's New Fracture Quartet, and her own trio
years.p: She plays on drummer Tim Daisy's 1000 Lights while leading Princess, Princess with bassist Toby Summerfield and drummer Frank Rosaly.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch · NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary
years.h: Predella Group: Vandermark, Jeff Parker and Jeb Bishop
years.p: She plays with [[Ken Vandermark|e5a4107f-5bb3-4f24-b9b7-927bb23840b5]] in his Predella Group, alongside guitarist [[Jeff Parker|4894f8eb-be75-4bd5-a3a3-7c20894439f9]] and trombonist Jeb Bishop, a murderers' row of Chicago improvisers.
years.xp: Branch also played with [[Nicole Mitchell|56f280d6-2f91-4af8-8a1a-fde9c9f2b876]] and formed an early trio with cellist Fred Lonberg-Holm, per NPR. She worked as a sound engineer and organizer around the same scene, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch · NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary
years.h: Baltimore: a master's degree, a record label, and a way out
years.p: She enrolls at Towson University and starts Pionic Records to release her group Bomb Shelter, then leaves the program after two years.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, six months after leaving Towson she moved to New York to seek treatment for heroin addiction. NPR's obituary says she relocated to Brooklyn around 2014 after treatment for substance use disorder. Wikipedia dates the Brooklyn move to spring 2015.

years.src: Wikipedia: International Anthem
years.h: International Anthem launches, in a Chicago bar
years.p: Drummer Scottie McNiece and engineer David Allen turn a live-jazz series into a label. Its first release is [[Rob Mazurek|73c34525-f9c6-4c33-9abe-007748aaebe5]]'s Alternative Moon Cycles.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, McNiece and Allen founded International Anthem in 2012 and launched it officially in 2014. Gilles Peterson named it his Label of the Year in 2020. Allen, the engineer, would later mix and master Branch's final album.

eras.title: Fly or Die
eras.text: Brooklyn, a pile of sideman gigs, and a one-off set with three Chicago friends that a label owner wouldn't let go. The first Fly or Die record turned a trumpeter known to insiders into someone critics had to rank.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch · Bandcamp Daily · NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary
years.h: Brooklyn: playing with everybody
years.p: She works with Fred Lonberg-Holm, Mike Pride, Luke Stewart and Jason Nazary, and appears on records by Never Enough Hope, Local H and the Atlas Moth.
years.xp: Bandcamp Daily adds James Brandon Lewis's Unruly Quintet, C'est Trois, and guest spots on albums by TV on the Radio and Talib Kweli. NPR says she lived in Red Hook.

years.cap: Trumpet Player Jaimie Branch at Jazzfestival Saalfelden 2019 · Wikimedia
q: I thought it was gonna be a one-off.
years.src: The Quietus · Bandcamp Daily
years.h: An improvised set with graphic scores becomes a record
years.p: Branch plays a set with Jason Ajemian, Chad Taylor and cellist [[Tomeka Reid|d91d6fca-ea9c-4a5d-a0ba-5a666c81cd51]]. International Anthem's Scottie McNiece is in the room and asks her to record.
years.xp:
The Quietus reports the band started in 2015, five or six months before the recording. Branch listened back to that first set and pulled the themes that became 'theme 001' and 'the storm' on the debut.

The other three were Chicago transplants too, per The Quietus.

years.src: The Quietus
years.h: Anteloper starts by accident, with a missing third member
years.p: Branch and drummer [[Jason Nazary|49a03c33-526e-46f9-b992-5b60c994b1ec]] both show up with electronics when a third player doesn't, and find they're a duo.
years.xp: Per The Quietus, she uses hardware synths and effects pedals and loopers, while Nazary works with modular and trigger setups.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch · Stereogum: Remembering · NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary
years.h: Fly or Die · International Anthem
years.p: Branch's first album under her own name: trumpet, voice, Reid's cello, Ajemian's bass, Taylor's drums. NPR Music put it in its Top 50 albums of 2017.
years.xp: Guests on the record include Matt Schneider, Ben LaMar Gay and Josh Berman, per Wikipedia. A Stereogum column remembering Branch after her death says the critic still stands by his pick of it as the best jazz album of 2017.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch
years.h: Kudu with Anteloper
years.p: The first record from Branch and Jason Nazary's electro-acoustic duo, also on International Anthem.

years.src: NPR: Chicago trumpeter jaimie branch delivers
years.h: In Paris, an improvised rant turns into a song
years.p: NPR says a rant she improvised on stage in Paris became the core of the political song on her next album, 'prayer for amerikkka'.
years.xp: NPR's Chicago coverage says she then quit her day job to focus on music full time.

eras.title: Bird dogs and alarms
eras.text: With a new cellist and a louder politics, Fly or Die gets its best-known record. Then the pandemic turns the band into a livestream, and then into a live album.

years.big: "It's a big f-you to all those people."
q: The trumpet is an alert, and we're sounding some alarms.
years.src: NPR: Chicago trumpeter jaimie branch delivers · The Quietus
years.h: 'prayer for amerikkka' on Fly or Die II
years.p: That's Branch's description of the record to NPR's local station. The two-part title track was inspired by a family her social worker mother assisted.
years.xp: Branch says the song is about the prisons along the border, which did not leave with any one administration. She explained the spelling as a comment on the nation's foundations. She said in the same interview that the trumpet is an alert, and the band was sounding some alarms.

years.src: NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary · The Quietus
years.h: Fly or Die II: Bird Dogs of Paradise · International Anthem
years.p: Cellist [[Lester St. Louis|cd3d55ee-51f0-4cb6-9ba7-2e0ceabe3b84]] takes Tomeka Reid's chair in the quartet. NPR says the record reached its 2019 Jazz Critics Poll top 10.
years.xp: Branch was obsessed with birds since childhood, The Quietus reports, and the covers of both Fly or Die albums show Colombian birds, a nod to her Colombian heritage. She traced part of it to a pet parakeet named Kiwi, and joked about it in the interview.
play: Fly or Die II: Bird Dogs of Paradise

years.h: Tour Beats Vol. 1: Anteloper on the road
years.p: Branch and Nazary's second Anteloper release on International Anthem, in the year Gilles Peterson gave the label his Label of the Year award.

eras.title: Omaha, then August
eras.text: The final year: a residency that produced the band's most ambitious material, a duo record, and an abrupt ending at 39.

years.cap: Jaimie Branch with Mars Williams' An Ayler Xmas, Club W71, Weikersheim · Wikimedia
years.src: The Fader · Bandcamp Daily · International Anthem
years.h: A residency in Omaha: the band's biggest material
years.p: The quartet records at the Bemis Center for Contemporary Arts. Branch wants longer forms, more modulations, more noise, more singing, per the label.
years.xp: The band's later statement says she always thought big. Per Bandcamp Daily, overdubs and mixing followed in July at International Anthem Studios in Chicago. Jason Ajemian told Bandcamp Daily she was all over the record, with only a couple of small things added afterward.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch
years.h: Pink Dolphins: the last Anteloper record
years.p: Branch and Jason Nazary's third International Anthem release as a duo.

years.src: NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary · Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch · Stereogum: Remembering
years.h: Branch dies at home in Red Hook at 39
years.p: International Anthem announced her death. Wikipedia states the cause as an accidental drug overdose; the label gave none, NPR reported at the time.
years.xp: Her sister Kate Branch said she was the bravest person she knew, on and off the stage. NPR also quotes Dave Douglas of FONT Music and Mark Christman of Ars Nova Workshop. A Stereogum writer said the news hit the younger jazz scene like a sledgehammer to the sternum.

eras.title: The record she left
eras.text: The band and Branch's family finish the last tweaks, and the album goes out as planned. Critics, several of them hearing her for the first time, rank it among the year's best.

years.big: "jaimie never had small ideas. She always thought big."
years.src: The Fader · International Anthem
yt: take over the world, official video
years.h: International Anthem announces the last Fly or Die album
years.p: The band's statement, issued with the announcement. The lead single 'take over the world' gets a video directed by Jon Philpot.
years.xp: The statement adds that the more people told her something was too difficult, the more determined she got. It promised longer forms, more modulations, more noise and more singing.

years.src: Album of the Year · Wikipedia: Fly or Die Fly or Die Fly or Die · International Anthem
years.h: Fly or Die Fly or Die Fly or Die ((world war))
years.p: Pitchfork's Andy Cush gave it 8.5 and Best New Album, and the site ranked it No. 28 of 2023.
years.xp:
Cush called it a heartbreaking glimpse of where she might have gone next and, more importantly, a joy to hear. Giovanni Russonello of the New York Times said it was as electrifying as the first two LPs, with a wider sonic horizon. Metacritic lists 95 from ten reviews, and The Guardian placed it No. 48 of 2023. Per Wikipedia it peaked at No. 20 on the UK Independent Albums chart.

The album was recorded in April 2022 at the Bemis Center in Omaha. It features Branch, Lester St. Louis, Jason Ajemian and Chad Taylor, plus trombonist Nick Broste, flutist Rob Frye and vocalist Akenya Seymour, per the label. David M. Allen mixed and mastered it.

years.h: Record release show at Roulette
years.p: The Fly or Die quartet celebrates the album in Brooklyn, and the night was filmed.
